answer.rationale: The incumbent has refused price renegotiation, and the finance mandate requires an 18% spend cut that only the low-cost vendor's quote can satisfy. memory_c2 demonstrates the low-cost vendor has proven execution capability (quick onboarding, accurate invoicing, cost reduction), and memory_c3 shows that single-vendor risk was mitigated successfully through second-sourcing when needed. However, the assembly line operates at 94% committed volume with no buffer, creating material risk if the switch causes any disruption. Verify memory_c2 to confirm the vendor's reliability track record and memory_c4 to understand whether renegotiation leverage exists (though the incumbent has already refused). The 14-day renewal window and mandate-only pricing from the low-cost vendor leave no realistic alternative. Scale as standard_experiment rather than broad rollout to monitor initial performance, but the financial imperative and vendor refusal eliminate defer_decision and make add_second_source insufficient. The high utilization rate flags downstream risk; any onboarding friction or quality variance could impact committed volume.
